summary: Master the art of prosecutorial decision-making and case management in financial crimes. Join our specialized training course to elevate your expertise.
lede: Prosecutorial decision-making and case management training provides a structured, repeatable approach to screening financial crime matters, prioritizing workloads, and making defensible decisions to charge, defer, or discontinue cases. You will learn to develop clear case theories, identify evidentiary gaps, reduce delays, and communicate next steps to investigators and supervisors. The course builds practical competence in managing evidence and disclosure, directing investigations, and preparing files for court or negotiation. Its hands-on approach reflects the document-heavy, technology-enabled, and politically sensitive nature of financial crime cases while supporting due process and trial readiness.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for professionals in the public sector, regulatory agencies, and financial intelligence units, who are entrusted with prosecuting and managing complex financial crime cases.
modules: Foundations of Prosecutorial Decision-Making in Financial Crimes
Developing Case Theory and Investigation Strategy
Digital Evidence and Cyber-Enabled Financial Crimes
Charge Selection, Counts, and Drafting Quality Charges
Case Management Tools for Complex Financial Crime Files
Working with Investigators, Regulators, and Experts
Risk, Ethics, and Bias in Prosecutorial Judgment
Court Readiness, Trial Strategy, and Case Resolution
Asset Recovery, Forfeiture, and Proceeds of Crime Linkage
Building a Culture of Performance and File Quality
prerequisites: Participants should have a background in law, criminal justice, or compliance. Prior experience with financial crime investigations or prosecutions is recommended.
